minor.issue: users.active counter uses {suspended: {$ne: true}, deleted_at: null}. Docs created before iter-7 lack the `deleted_at` field entirely and match `deleted_at: null` in Mongo (Mongo equality with null matches missing) — OK today but brittle: a future user doc that intentionally sets deleted_at to a Falsy-non-null value (e.g. empty string) would be miscounted. Consider `{deleted_at: {$in: [null, undefined]}}` or use a stable `state` field.

Accepts role='superadmin' from the request body (see body.role in ('owner','marketer','viewer','superadmin')). Any existing superadmin can therefore create another superadmin — arguably intended, but there is no separate audit gate. Consider requiring an env-var-guarded feature flag or a second-superadmin confirmation.

Returns password_hash-free rows but includes `created_by_admin`, `suspended_at` etc. that are useful; however the `state` field is derived on every call. If a doc has `suspended: true` AND `deleted_at` set, `state` shows 'deleted' (which is fine) — but the underlying `suspended: true` remains after restore (restore only unsets deleted_at + suspended flag). Verified restore does clear both. No action.

verify_api_key iterates ALL non-revoked keys with bcrypt.checkpw per-lookup. This is O(N × bcrypt_cost) per request — at ~10 rounds bcrypt each check costs ~10-40ms. With >100 active keys latency will visibly grow. Consider indexing keys by a fast prefix (`pk_live_XXXXX` — first 8 chars of key + full bcrypt hash) for lookup narrowing, or use HMAC-SHA256(secret, key) with a constant-time compare instead of bcrypt.

Preview stored on the workspace as `secret[:14] + '…'` where `secret` is the plaintext. Good for the /pos/secrets response, but the plaintext prefix is now persistent in the DB (only the middle+suffix are encrypted). Consider deriving the preview from a deterministic hash instead so no plaintext bytes touch persistent storage.
Only owners can clear (matches rotate). No audit trail is written — consider logging to db.admin_logs (or workspace_logs) for compliance.

CARRY-OVER (from iter-5/6): Split /app/backend/server.py — now 2744 lines — into routers/{auth,coupons,pos,journeys,ai,analytics,exports,embed,customers,admin,library}.py. This iteration alone added ~300 LOC (admin+library+encrypt helpers+api-key auth).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: 2441 → 2744 lines (+303 LOC). Router split now clearly overdue; the admin section (~135 LOC), library (~75), pk_live auth (~30), and encrypt helpers (~15) are cleanly separable modules.

Fernet key derivation `Fernet(base64.urlsafe_b64encode(sha256(JWT_SECRET).digest()))` is deterministic across restarts — good. However rotating JWT_SECRET now invalidates ALL stored encrypted webhook_secrets (they'll fail decrypt_str → return None → workaround: server falls back to trust-mode silently, which is a SECURITY REGRESSION during JWT_SECRET rotation). Consider a dedicated FERNET_KEY env var so JWT and webhook-encryption keys can rotate independently, and log a warning when decrypt_str returns None for a configured secret.

verify_api_key falls back to iterating db.api_keys.find({revoked: {$ne: True}}) then bcrypt.checkpw per row. O(N) bcrypt scan is fine for MVP but will not scale past ~100 active keys per environment. Recommend keeping the first 12 chars of the pk_live_ token as a plaintext prefix column (e.g. `key_prefix`), indexed, and only bcrypt-check that single candidate.
admin_create_user hashes the new user's password inline via hash_password (bcrypt gensalt) — same as /auth/register. Consistent. Good.

The Admin Portal frontend at /admin renders unconditionally for authenticated users — only backend 403s block data. This surfaces confusing 5-parallel-403 spam in console for any non-superadmin who reaches /admin (bookmark, link click). Add a client-side guard: `if (user.role !== 'superadmin') return <Navigate to='/' />`.

In the sidebar filter `NAV.filter((n) => !n.superadmin || user?.role === 'superadmin')` the `user?.role` is optional-chained — on first render (before AuthContext hydrates) the Admin link is hidden even for superadmin. Not a bug (it reappears once user is loaded), but explains the transient flicker; if desired, defer sidebar render until `user` is truthy.
webhook_secrets stores three per-provider keys: `<provider>` (Fernet-encrypted), `<provider>_rotated_at`, `<provider>_preview`. clear_pos_secret unsets all three via $unset — verified. Good.

COUPON_LIBRARY is a static Python list — served fresh on every /api/library/coupon-types call. Consider caching (functools.lru_cache) or moving to a JSON asset served with far-future Cache-Control since it never changes at runtime.

admin_stats query `{deleted_at: null}` relies on Mongo equality-with-null-matches-missing-field semantics — works, but write it as `{deleted_at: {$in: [null]}}` OR `{$or: [{deleted_at: null}, {deleted_at: {$exists: false}}]}` to make intent explicit.
